identity.name: Calcium acetate
identity.chemical_class: Calcium salt of acetic acid (organic acetate salt)

function.mechanism: Acts as an acetate buffering/pH-control salt and preservative contributor; calcium ion supports firmness and texture/stabilization functions.
common_food_categories: other foods at very low CGMP levels

adi.basis: No published EFSA food-additive re-evaluation ADI entry identified for E263 in the current EU summary table; E263 listed as permitted and re-evaluation shown as not completed.

efsa.key_finding: E263 (calcium acetate) appears in the EU summary table of permitted additives; EFSA food-additive re-evaluation fields are blank for E263 as of the 18 Feb 2026 status table.

fda.notes: In Part 184 (direct food substances affirmed as GRAS); use is under CGMP with listed maximum as-served levels (e.g., 0.2% baked goods, 0.02% cheese, 0.0001% all other categories).

concerns.summary: Therapeutic-dose calcium-based phosphate binder literature in CKD/dialysis populations reports higher hypercalcemia risk compared with some non-calcium binders; this reflects medicinal high-dose exposure rather than typical food-additive intake.
Historical JECFA toxicology reported limited direct calcium acetate toxicity data; acetate and calcium were considered physiologic moieties, with ADI set to not limited.

no_concern_confirmed: No IARC classification entry found for calcium acetate (name or CAS 62-54-4) in the current IARC list data bundle.
JECFA record lists ADI as not limited.
FDA affirms GRAS status under specified conditions of use in 21 CFR 184.1185.

populations: No general-population ADI exceedance signal identified from checked regulatory sources
adi_exceedance.notes: JECFA ADI is non-numerical (not limited). EFSA numerical ADI for E263 food-additive re-evaluation was not identified in the current EU summary table.

risk_assessment.rationale: Regulatory status is broadly permissive (FDA GRAS, JECFA ADI not limited, EU permitted listing), with no IARC carcinogenic classification identified. Main safety caveat comes from high-dose clinical calcium-binder use (hypercalcemia risk), which is not directly representative of normal food-additive exposure.
key_factors: FDA GRAS with explicit CGMP and category-level limits
JECFA ADI not limited and long history of use
No IARC listing for calcium acetate/CAS 62-54-4
EFSA food-additive re-evaluation entry for E263 not found as completed in current EU summary table
High-dose CKD therapeutic data indicate calcium-load caution in susceptible groups
